units: ₹ crore unless stated. IMPORTANT: the company's headline 'revenue' (FY26 ₹9,018 cr; Q1FY27 ₹2,627 cr) is GROSS of GST. The audited P&L, Screener, CRISIL and this model use NET revenue (FY26 ₹8,286 cr; Q1FY27 ₹2,387 cr). Company EBITDA (FY26 ₹1,172 cr) ≈ Screener operating profit (₹1,168 cr).

business.summary: Benzene- and toluene-based specialty chemical intermediates: nitrochlorobenzenes (NCB), dichlorobenzenes (DCB), hydrogenation products (chloroanilines), phenylenediamines (PDA), nitrotoluenes (NT), ethylation products (MEA/DEA), sulphuric-acid derivatives, and fuel additives (MMA, monomethyl aniline, an octane booster). 100+ products, 16 plants in Gujarat and Maharashtra (Vapi, Jhagadia, Dahej, Kutch, Tarapur), 5,800+ employees, 1,100+ customers in 60+ countries.

marketPosition.value: Claims #1 globally in DCB, top 2 in hydrogenation, top 3 in NCB, and 4th globally in ~75% of its portfolio (AR26); CRISIL: largest producer of benzene derivatives in India with 25-40% global share across products

customers.value: No customer ≥10% of revenue (FY25, FY26). Logos include BASF, Syngenta, DuPont, Bayer, SABIC, Eastman, Nouryon, FMC, Clariant, Celanese, UPL, ADNOC, IndianOil, HPCL, BPCL, Halliburton

segmentReporting.value: One reportable segment under Ind AS 108; no segment results or assets. End-use mix and energy / non-energy volume growth are given only in presentations.

rawMaterials.value: Benzene (domestic), toluene, aniline (for MMA; imported mainly from China), sulphur, methanol, chlorine (pipeline from DCM Shriram for Zone IV), nitric acid (20-year supply from Deepak Fertilisers since Apr-2023). Domestic RM inventory 7-15 days; imported 1-1.5 months.

endUseMix._note: % of company (gross) revenue, from results presentations. Gross revenue ₹ cr in 'grossRev'.

energyRevenueNetFY26.note: Energy share 15% of revenue in FY23 → 43% in FY26

domesticExportQ1FY27.note: Domestic % / export % of each end use, Q1FY27

q1fy27.value: Exports 59% of revenue; Middle East fell from ~15% of revenue to 2% (West Asia conflict); volumes redirected to the US, Europe and Africa

usExposure.value: US ~18% of FY25 turnover (MMA, PDA chain, dimethyl sulphate, ONA, DCB); about half of US sales were tariff-exempt; 50% tariff on the rest until the India-US deal cut it to ~18%

volumes._note: Production by product group, kT (AGM presentation FY22-FY26; quarterly from Q3FY26/Q4FY26 presentations). From Q1FY27 the company stopped disclosing product volumes and gives only energy / non-energy growth and utilisation bands.

fy26Growth.value: Volumes +39% while blended realisations fell 25% (CRISIL); company: volumes +30%+, fuel-additive production +81%

energy.what: Fuel additives, mainly MMA (monomethyl aniline), a high-octane gasoline booster blended at below 1-2% by refiners and blenders, plus calcium chloride. Not methyl methacrylate and not fuel trading. Demand and price track the gasoline-naphtha crack and aniline (the raw material).
energy.history: ~15% of revenue in FY22; scaled up from FY24 under a 4-year ₹6,000 cr+ contract (Jan-2024) with a multinational conglomerate; 43% of FY26 revenue.
energy.q1fy27: Energy volumes −17% QoQ, +57% YoY; Middle East share of company revenue fell from ~15% to 2%. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl; management expects high utilisation of 360 kT 'in this quarter itself' and a broader 3-5 product fuel-additive basket over 12 months. Winter weakness from late October.
energy.competition: CEO: 'more than two or three players in India' and 'more than 2 or 3 players in China' already compete; Aarti claims market leadership and top-decile cost.

steadyStateShare.value: 30-40% of revenue once Zone IV ramps up

energy.marginDisclosure: Not disclosed. The 2024 contract was guided at a 15-17% margin at constant prices (Feb-2024 call).

contracts.name: LTC-1 (agro intermediate for dicamba, 2,5-DCP chain)
contracts.status: 10-year contract cancelled by the customer in Jun-2020; $120 mn compensation. FY22 revenue/EBITDA include ₹631 cr of termination income; ₹138 cr of shortfall fees in FY22. The ~₹500 cr plant has been underutilised since; about 50% of it now makes a dicamba intermediate with steady volumes (May-2026).

contracts.name: LTC-2 (20-year polymer intermediate, global major)
contracts.status: Customer-funded (~₹400-450 cr of advances), ~₹500 cr revenue a year, EBITDA protected regardless of volume; running as per contract.

contracts.name: LTC-3 (10-year advanced polymer intermediate, US major)
contracts.status: Commissioned Q3FY23; ramp-up ~2 years late, peak expected ~FY27.

contracts.name: LTC-4 (Dec-2023, 9-year herbicide intermediate)
contracts.status: ₹3,000 cr+ revenue potential over 9 years at ~20% margin; FY25 guided ₹300 cr then cut to ~₹250 cr; margins below original expectation (May-2026).

contracts.name: LTC-5 (Jan-2024, 4-year fuel-additive contract)
contracts.status: ₹6,000 cr+ over 4 years with a multinational conglomerate; target volumes met in CY2025 on a yearly basis.

contracts.name: Nitric acid supply (Deepak Fertilisers, 20 years, from Apr-2023)
contracts.status: Operating as per contract; replaced a planned captive plant.

contracts.name: Backward-integration amendment (Mar-2026)
contracts.status: Existing exclusive contract with a leading global chemical company amended: Aarti will make a significant part of the feedstock the customer now supplies, adding fixed margin over the residual 15 years; capex ₹200-250 cr over two years; commissioning Sep-Oct 2027.

contracts.name: $150 mn agro supply contract (Mar-2026)
contracts.status: Multi-year supply to a top global agrochemical innovator until Mar-2030, existing product, no significant capex; volumes from FY27.

contracts.name: No take-or-pay on new projects
contracts.status: None of the new projects (MPP, PEDA, Zone IV) has a take-or-pay contract (Nov-2025 call).

fy28.value: EBITDA ₹1,800-2,200 cr by FY28, debt/EBITDA <2.5x, ROCE >15%. Bridge from FY25: cost optimisation ₹150-200 cr, volume and margin ramp-up ₹350-550 cr, capex-led growth ₹300-450 cr. First given Nov-2024; reaffirmed every quarter; includes Augene JV EBITDA.

zoneIVDelay.value: Zone IV delayed 3-4 months (May-2026), then 'by 2 quarters' (Jul-2026) due to labour shortages and war-related issues; commissioned in phases in FY27, ramp-up over FY28-FY29; 5-10 products this year, 25-30 by FY28. CEO: the delay 'might lead to a bit slower ramp-up' than the FY27-28 plan.

fy27.value: No annual EBITDA guidance (dropped in 2025). Capex ₹700-800 cr; tax rate 10-15%; net debt to fall in FY27 (internal target).

trackRecord.first: No annual guidance; 20-25% EBITDA CAGR goal (Aug-2024) implies ~₹1,220 cr

trackRecord.last: Reaffirmed Jul-2026 despite Zone IV delay

guidance.marginTargets: Feb-2024: 18-20% EBITDA margin at ₹1,700 cr EBITDA (FY25 actual 13.7%); FY28 bridge based on a 14-15% margin.

q1fy27.drivers: Revenue growth 'primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to customers'; volumes −12% QoQ (energy −17%, non-energy −7%), +57% / +12% YoY. EBITDA helped by monetising low-cost inventory and FX gains: ₹50-60 cr (CEO); CRISIL: underlying margin ~14%. Working capital and debt rose with input prices and long-haul exports. NCB chain margins recovered after China removed export VAT rebates (from Apr-2026). PDA structurally weak ('technological disadvantage'); NT margins suppressed by isomer imbalance. Capex ₹180 cr in Q1; FY27 ₹700-800 cr on track; capex intensity to fall 'significantly' from FY28.
q1fy27.otherNews: Board approved Suyog Kotecha as MD & CEO from 1-Oct-2026 and the move of promoter executive directors (Rajendra, Rashesh and Renil Gogri) to non-executive roles, subject to AGM approval (21-Sep-2026). Fuel-additive capacity 360 kTPA completed Jul-2026. Augene JV commissioning in Q2FY27 (steady-state revenue ₹300-400 cr; consolidated at PAT level). Re Aarti recycling JV H2FY27 (3-month delay). Plans to set up a subsidiary in China. EcoVadis Platinum.

q4fy26.notes: Finance cost included a ₹39 cr revaluation loss on an unhedged $87 mn loan. Exports ~57% of revenue; freight costs up. Net debt ~₹4,300 cr (3.6x EBITDA); gross debt ₹4,921 cr including a term loan disbursed in the last days of March. FY26 capex ₹1,125 cr; FY27 ₹700-800 cr (Zone IV completion, backward-integration project, ~₹150 cr maintenance). Gross block to reach ₹9,500-10,000 cr by end-FY27. Target working-capital cycle 55-60 days. Tax 9-15% while Zone IV tax depreciation lasts. FY26 tax credit came from favourable tax rulings and deferred-tax adjustments.

capex.historyNote: Company figures (AGM / AR26 highlights); FY22 from Screener cash flow. ~₹7,640 cr over FY21-26 (Screener cash flow).
capex.beyond: CRISIL: ₹200-250 cr a year from FY28
capex.zoneIV: Jhagadia greenfield, ₹1,600-1,800 cr: calcium chloride (commercialised), multipurpose plant (first product Aug-2026), PEDA 4,000 TPA (market seeding), and five chemistry blocks (chlorotoluene, photochlorination, hydrolysis, nitration); 97% of equipment erected, 85% of piping done (Jul-2026). Originally slated for FY25-FY26. Stated aspiration: ₹2,000 cr+ revenue at 25-30% EBITDA margin (older calls).

balanceSheet.liquidity: Unencumbered liquid surplus ₹310 cr (30-Jun-2026); bank-limit use 75% (12 months to Jul-2026); repayments ₹248-350 cr a year vs expected cash accrual ₹900-1,300 cr a year (FY27-29).
balanceSheet.q1fy27: Working capital rose further in Q1FY27 (elevated feedstock prices, long-haul DAP exports); debt and finance costs increased (amount not disclosed).
balanceSheet.fxLoan: ~$87 mn unhedged foreign-currency term loan (IFC green loan $130 mn, SOFR+100bp, repayable to FY34)

ratings.note: Outlook Negative since 11-Sep-2025: geopolitics and working capital could delay deleveraging. Downgrade if margin <12-13% or gross debt/EBITDA >3.6x; upgrade if <2.75x.
Deleveraging 12-15 months later than envisaged; net leverage >3.0x through FY27; free cash flow negative FY26-27, positive FY28. Gross margin 42% (FY23) → 34% (9MFY26) vs ~45% decadal average.

tax.fy26: Total tax −₹54 cr on PBT ₹365 cr (−14.9%): income-tax depreciation on new capacity wipes out normal tax, MAT paid (₹64 cr) is booked as a MAT-credit asset, and deferred-tax assets on tax losses (₹324 cr) exceed the deferred-tax liability on depreciation (₹270 cr). Exceptional items: +₹28.5 cr interest on tax orders, −₹15.4 cr labour codes, −₹6.7 cr land-advance provision.
tax.guidance: 9-15% effective rate while Zone IV tax depreciation lasts

history.event: Incorporated as Aarti Organic Pvt Ltd by first-generation technocrats (Gogri family); first NCB unit at Sarigam (1986)
Two large multi-year contracts (FY18) and a third (FY19); ₹750 cr QIP (FY19)
Customer cancels a 10-year dicamba-intermediate contract; $120 mn compensation (₹631 cr booked in FY22 revenue)
1:1 bonus; ₹1,200 cr QIP at ₹855 a share
Pharma business demerged into Aarti Pharmalabs (appointed date 1-Jul-2021, record date 20-Oct-2022, listed 30-Jan-2023); past financials recast
20-year nitric acid supply deal with Deepak Fertilisers replaces a captive plant
9-year ₹3,000 cr+ herbicide-intermediate contract; 4-year ₹6,000 cr+ fuel-additive contract
Suyog Kotecha (ex-Reliance, McKinsey) joins as ED & CEO
Augene JV (50:50, amine derivatives; announced with UPL, partner now named Superform Chemistries) and Re Aarti plastic-recycling JV with Re Sustainability
FY25 EBITDA guidance (₹1,450-1,700 cr) withdrawn; Nov-2024: FY28 target of ₹1,800-2,200 cr
CRISIL outlook to Negative; India Ratings follows (Feb-2026)
Backward-integration amendment (15-year residual) and $150 mn agro supply contract
Fuel-additive capacity 360 kTPA; Q1FY27 record revenue on pass-through of input prices
43rd AGM (21-Sep): resolutions for Suyog Kotecha as MD from 1-Oct-2026 and Gogri executives to non-executive roles

points: Headline revenue includes GST (₹732 cr in FY26); the net figure is ₹8,286 cr.
FY26 PAT helped by a tax credit (effective rate −15%) and ₹28.5 cr of interest on tax refunds (exceptional).
Q1FY27 EBITDA includes ₹50-60 cr of inventory and FX gains; FX on loans sits in finance cost (₹64 cr loss in FY26) while FX on trade sits in EBITDA.
Receivables up from ₹786 cr to ₹1,403 cr in FY26; operating cash flow fell from ₹1,238 cr to ₹781 cr.
Supplier-finance arrangements ₹246 cr inside payables; unsecured short-term bank debt up from ₹50 cr to ₹1,000 cr.
Contract shortfall fees (₹24 cr FY26, ₹72 cr FY25) are booked as other operating revenue.
FY22 includes ₹631 cr of contract-termination income inside revenue and EBITDA.
